verdicts.summary: If the secret store cannot be read, the changes stream sends unmaterialized settings to the provider registry. Antigravity is then rebuilt with the redaction marker as its API key.
verdicts.scenario: 1) An Antigravity instance has authMethod gemini-api-key and a saved apiKey. After this commit, settings.json and the cache hold `••••••`. 2) Any settings update or file-watch revalidate emits a change. 3) secretStore.get fails during materializeSettingsSecrets. 4) materializeChanges logs a warning and emits the raw settings (serverSettings.ts:916). 5) ProviderInstanceRegistryHydration reconciles with config.apiKey = `••••••`. AntigravityDriver passes it on, the auth check sees a non-empty key, and antigravityEnvironment sets GEMINI_API_KEY=`••••••`. Before this commit the key was plaintext in the cache, so this failure could not swap it.
verdicts.consequence: The Antigravity provider reports itself configured, but every session fails to authenticate until the next successful change event. No error points at the secret store.

verdicts.summary: The load-time migration rewrites the Antigravity apiKey in settings.json to the marker. A server from before this commit reads the marker as the real key.
verdicts.scenario: 1) A user has a plaintext Antigravity apiKey in settings.json. 2) They start this version. moveInlineSettingsSecrets stores the key and writeSettingsAtomically writes `••••••` (serverSettings.ts:714-716, 850). 3) They roll back to the parent commit. The old materialize handled only env vars, usage keys and host slots (diff lines 470-527), not provider config. So the old AntigravityDriver gets apiKey=`••••••`. The plaintext key is no longer in the file.
verdicts.consequence: After a downgrade, Antigravity API-key and Agent Platform auth fail. The user has to enter the key again because it is gone from settings.json.

verdicts.summary: The note says the old code also ignored an empty commit. That is wrong for Antigravity apiKey: it was not a secret field before, so emptying the input cleared it. After this commit a saved key cannot be cleared from the settings UI.
verdicts.scenario: 1) A user saves an Antigravity API key with authMethod agent-platform. 2) They later want project/location auth, so they set gcpProject and gcpLocation and try to remove the key. 3) The settings branch renders SecretInput with value="" (ProviderSettingsForm.tsx:415-424). Clearing the input commits nothing: DraftInput only commits when the draft changes, and SecretInput drops `configured && next===""`. There is no clear button. 4) Before this commit the field had no secret flag, so it rendered a DraftInput holding the saved value. Emptying it called nextProviderConfigWithFieldValue, which drops the key because clearWhenEmpty is omit (diff 1256-1300, 1509-1519). 5) While apiKey is set, antigravityEnvironment always sends GOOGLE_API_KEY, which the agent prefers over the GCP pair.
verdicts.consequence: A user cannot remove a saved Antigravity API key, and so cannot switch Agent Platform to project/location auth, without deleting the whole provider instance.

verdicts.summary: The settingsSecret annotation survives withDecodingDefault. decodeTo keeps the `to` schema and only replaces its encoding, and copy preserves context. A later annotateKey merges into that context.
verdicts.scenario: Tried Antigravity apiKey and GitCafe token, where secretSetting comes before withDecodingDefault. withDecodingDefault calls decodeTo(self) (Schema.ts:5911). That calls SchemaAST.decodeTo, then appendTransformation, then replaceEncoding(to, ...) (SchemaAST.ts:4374). That calls copy, which keeps `to.context` because Object.assign copies every field (4239). The following annotateKey spreads the existing context annotations (4408). resolveAnnotationsKey reads ast.context.annotations (Schema.ts:15959). The server test at serverSettings.test.ts:1512-1524 also asserts the Antigravity key is redacted.
